narrative:
The model estimates a 62% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while at your current employer. Most employees predicted to stay (77%) had no such external offers, so this factor significantly pushes the prediction toward you leaving.

Next, your 6-10 years of experience in your current role works in your favor. This is longer than the typical tenure among those expected to stay, which helps pull the prediction back toward staying with the organization.

Your overall career experience of 6-10 years also contributes, though it leans toward leaving. While many who are predicted to stay have shorter overall experience (50% have 1-5 years), your mid-range total experience slightly increases the estimated risk of departure.

Taken together, the external opportunities outweigh the stabilizing effect of your tenure here, leading to the decision against promotion. The organization should discuss your career goals with you directly and explore ways to match external offers or increase your sense of long-term stability. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your ambitions. (218 words)
